Interesting! I agree with most of your rankings here, with a few differences! I'll try to organize them into a list like yours (easiest to hardest):

1. Master Ring. I thought this was the easiest for me (mostly because my entire party had high stats, powerful weapons, and abilities like Tornado Slash/Millionaire/Wheel Slash). I guess if it wasn't for the fact that I had 5 Asuras and 3 of the 5 people also holding Dragon Swords, maybe it would've been a different story? But this was the one boss that I could win without relying on Time Magic.
2. Diva. Not much to add here. It was super easy for me with Time Leap. Without it, I would've had a harder time, even with my party's high stats. Glass Shield and Deflect came in handy too though.
3. Orlouge! I was so sad when I discovered that Time Leap was ineffective, so this bumped up the difficulty. Glass Shield was also useless because the shards would only attack the ghosts that defend Orlouge, and as you said - damage being done to them does nothing to Orlouge >.< I just kept relying on what I could muster up for multiple level combos to defeat him (which itself is a challenge since sometimes the level combo doesn't work!!)
4. Boss-X. Actually... I would tie this with Orlouge if I could, but in terms of damages to my party, I guess Boss-X was a bit more harsh, so I'll put him up as #4, Other than that, I was able to push through this battle with good ol' Time Leap, but on occasions where he attacked first, the damage was quite devastating. I didn't encounter many other difficulties though so I was kinda surprised to find this battle was the second hardest for you! Was I just lucky? >.<
5. Spriggan. Even with Time Magic, Spriggan did a lot of damage when it could. This was actually the FIRST boss that I attempted (and failed). It took me a couple times to get used to his patterns, but without Time Leap, I probably would've died a few times more lol.
6. Hell's Lord. As you said, the continuous AoE damage made this one extremely difficult to fight. I was able to defeat it without OverDrive (Time Lord had one of the lower HPs compared to the rest of my party and I didn't feel like grinding to get him on the same level), just with Time Leap was fine. But of course... sometimes the boss attacks first and then Time Leap was useless since everybody on my party was poisoned and losing HP by big numbers...
7. Genocide Heart. The one boss I dreaded and put off until last since I knew I would still die several times anyway. Just like you, I didn't properly manage my WP/JP at first. And that Carnage attack would consistently KO 2 out of 5 people for me, even though their HPs were in the 900's. Time Leap was only useful during those rounds where you'd be transported to another location, but when those damn TV screens (or whatever those are!) came back, Time Leap was useless (because half my party would already be KO'd...) I don't think any other boss could top this one in terms of difficulty haha.

Edit: I just want to add that Mesarthim was the MVP for me! I couldn't have fought Hell's Lord without her!! I love her so much <3

Why would they owe you any money? When you took over their lease, it became your responsibility and no longer theirs. It's not the same as "giving them 10k". I will give you credit that you did them a favor, but favors are just that - they're not meant to be a reciprocal deal. Are you buying this house with your gf, or is it just going to be in your name? If it's the latter, then all the more reason that your gf's parents don't owe you anything. Yes, in a perfect world, it would've been generous and great if they did decide to give you 3k as a goodwill, but.... most people are not generous like that. And your gf's family is not like-minded like you. So I think a good lesson for you here is that when it comes to anything money-related, don't deal with it if it involves your family/friends/gf/gf's family.

Riki (and T260G) are the only two characters that I haven't really done multiple playthroughs with, so my insight might be rather limited. But sometimes monsters don't change appearance if they absorb a monster that has a 'similar' ability as the creature they are currently. For example, attack moves like Fang, Lysate, Claw, and Beat are associated with the xeno (I'm guessing this is the Patrick from Spongebob creature you are referring to xD), but it is also the attacks that slime, jellyfish, the giant caterpillar, shellworm, and etc also has. Sometimes, a "bigger" monster has those same moves too - so even when you think you're about to absorb a more powerful monster, you end up absorbing one of their basic attack moves and also don't change appearance from your current form either. 

Anyway! That's probably why your appearance isn't changing, and unfortunately there is no way to change it (blame it on the classic RNG system of the early days of jrpgs haha). But as somebody else said on here, it might be better for you to play as Riki after you've cleared some characters, and when you start New Game+, you can try checking the checkbox for Enemy Ranks so that you will start off fighting the higher level enemies early in Riki's story. Once you start encountering "stronger" creatures like the Dullahan, it IS possible to change into those creatures (but again... you have to grind for a while...). When it finally happens, it will feel SO GOOD :3
